theme: Preservation of local acquired data on D: with historical checkout paths
question: Can bulk local data be moved off C: while retaining exact source bytes and historical project paths?
outcome: 187,131 accessible files, 35,099,820,039 bytes, matched destination SHA-256 before their C: copies were removed. Nine directory junctions and 434 file links retain paths. Bulk data are at D:/projects/indus_valley_script. One plotting environment with 14 inaccessible directories and one inaccessible 110-byte file is preserved intact on C:. Entry documents and all seven repository task skills identify the new root.
challenge: Long Windows paths, denied ACLs, a failed early hashing run, and navigation tools that resolved junction targets outside the checkout.
remedy: Extended-length path inventory; incremental file hashes; whole-environment preservation for inaccessible material; destination verification before native PowerShell removal; explicit checked source and target roots; storage-aware repository-relative path validation.
retry_when: A storage target is unavailable, restoration is required, or a new bulk tree must be relocated. Keep the external manifest and backup; do not replace a missing junction with a C: data directory.
